data.exact_reserve_text: The 2020 year of account has produced a net profit of $20.1m, inclusive of favourable claims development during the 2023 calendar year of $17.8m. The total estimate for insurance losses incurred but not reported at 31 December 2023 is $384.3m (2022: $414.4m).

prior_year_events.impact_description: Contributed 12.8 percentage points to the equivalent 2022 catastrophe claims ratio and materially increased 2022 catastrophe claims experience.
Materially impacted the loss ratio for prior years referenced by the report.
Referenced as one of the events that materially impacted prior year loss ratios.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced aggregate favourable prior-year development of approximately $38.7m (a ~6.5% release relative to opening gross claims outstanding of $598.6m). The release was driven by favourable claims development on older years (notably a $17.8m favourable development on the 2020 year), lower-than-expected catastrophe severity relative to prior estimates and reductions in IBNR. The portfolio improvements follow underwriting de-risking actions and were partially offset by continued convective and winter storm activity in the current year.
raw_causal_phrases: favourable claims development during the 2023 calendar year of $17.8m.
The total estimate for insurance losses incurred but not reported at 31 December 2023 is $384.3m (2022: $414.4m).
After the first three years of the Syndicate being impacted by US catastrophes, the 2023 loss ratio is an improvement on the prior year and reflects the underwriting actions taken on the portfolio.
The current year catastrophe claims ratio is 9.4% which has reduced from 17.5% in 2022, albeit the current year includes a higher frequency of convective and winter storms.
data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development was not stated as a single gross figure in a labelled 'movement in prior years' note. The prior-year movement (-38.7) was calculated from the gross claims development triangle (gross earned ultimate claims by underwriting year) by comparing the current estimate to the prior diagonal for underwriting years <= 2021. The report does explicitly state a $17.8m favourable development on the 2020 year and shows IBNR falling from $414.4m to $384.3m; these corroborate the triangle-based calculation. Amounts and directions are in the report's native currency (USD).
